summary: This PR builds out the 5 phase_8 prompt-distribution engines (translation, localization, marketplace, export, import) with reasonable service/API/schema structure and real unit tests, and its final commit specifically claims to fix the RLS/GRANT gap flagged by audit for the 3 new tables (prompt_translations, prompt_localizations, prompt_marketplace_listings) -- but the fix is incomplete and the core write paths of the feature will still fail once this migration is applied live: the new migration (drizzle/0268) only creates a SELECT policy for app_runtime on all three tables (copying the same latent-bug pattern already present in the older drizzle/0019 precedent for prompt_versions), with no INSERT policy on any of the three tables and no UPDATE policy on prompt_marketplace_listings, so every db.insert()/db.update() call from the new services will be rejected by Postgres RLS ('new row violates row-level security policy') even though the table-level GRANTs otherwise permit it. Worse, the table-level GRANTs themselves are also incomplete: prompt_translations and prompt_localizations only grant SELECT+INSERT to app_runtime, but prompt-translation-service.ts's force-retranslate path and prompt-localization-service.ts's force-relocalize path both call db.update() on these exact tables, which will fail with a hard permission-denied error, not just an RLS violation. Net effect: translate (force), localize (force), publish-to-marketplace, and unlist-from-marketplace will all error out in production despite this commit's stated purpose being exactly to prevent that class of failure. Everything else in the diff (schema, services, tests, permission gating at veridian_admin, no workflow-file changes) looks sound, but this is a functional regression in the one thing this specific commit was supposed to fix, so it should not be merged as-is.
issues: drizzle/0268_prompt_translation_localization_marketplace.sql only defines a 'FOR SELECT TO app_runtime USING (true)' policy for prompt_translations, prompt_localizations, and prompt_marketplace_listings -- there is no INSERT policy (any table) or UPDATE policy (prompt_marketplace_listings) for app_runtime, so RLS will reject every db.insert()/db.update() call the new services make (translatePromptVersion, localizePromptVersion, publishToMarketplace, unlistFromMarketplace) even though the surrounding GRANT statements are otherwise correct for those operations. This is the same broken pattern already latent in drizzle/0019's prompt_versions GRANT (INSERT granted with no matching INSERT/ALL policy for app_runtime) -- confirmed app_runtime is NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS per drizzle/0215's own comment, so this isn't a theoretical concern.

GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON compliance.prompt_translations TO app_runtime and the identical line for prompt_localizations omit UPDATE, but prompt-translation-service.ts:92 and prompt-localization-service.ts:110 both do db.update(...) on these exact tables (the force=true / re-localize path). This will fail with a table-level permission-denied error, independent of the RLS-policy gap above.

Given this commit's own stated purpose was closing an audit-flagged RLS/GRANT gap for these 3 tables (per the migration's own header comment: 'every read/write from the 5 new API routes would have failed with permission-denied once this migration was applied live'), shipping it with write paths still broken means the fix does not actually achieve its goal -- reads work, writes do not.
